files.purpose: MarkdownView.swift is the chat's markdown renderer and most of its inline machinery. MarkdownView parses a message into blocks through a bounded cache (800 finished texts) and 48 streaming slots that re-parse only the block being extended, warms finished messages off the main thread, and draws a finished reply as ProseRunView runs plus standalone blocks and a streaming reply block by block with the settled/streaming flags. MarkdownBlockView draws each block: headings, paragraphs routed between the native link paragraph and veiled text by links, head mentions, list depth and streaming, the lead's `hydra` delegation card, code, list markers, quotes, tables and rules. RichLink builds pretty link titles, bare-domain autolinks and favicon/video asset keys. FaviconCache fetches /favicon.ico only for public hosts and strips white plates. InlineText picks the AppKit link paragraph or a veiled Text. CodeBlock collapses at 120 lines, TableBlock at 30 rows, and CopyButton copies through ProseReflow. At B3 the file stops naming the App-layer HydraDelegationBlock. The card now comes through the MarkdownDelegationCard.render hook that AppDelegate sets at launch. Mention scanning moves to MentionScanner and link hover moves to LinkHoverModifier. InlineText now sends any link, including a host-less local file link, to the native paragraph, and RichLink's streaming slots rise from 4 to 48.

feature_notes: B3 327-333 and 505-509 (commit d70cff8fe 'layer rules restored'): MarkdownBlockView no longer names HydraDelegationBlock, an App view. The code case now needs a registered renderer (`let delegationRenderer = MarkdownDelegationCard.render`) and calls `delegationRenderer(code, info != "hydra")`. AppDelegate.applicationDidFinishLaunching sets the hook (AppDelegate.swift:14) before any window is shown. New source branch: when render is nil, a hydra, hydra-sent or hydra-leaving block falls through to CodeBlock. The comment says "until then the block reads as code". transition(for:) (51-56) still gives such a block the asymmetric transition. The opacity, scale and hit-testing of the leaving card are unchanged.

B3 418-420, 425, 439: the two inline word-bounded, longest-first scans (B2 419-441 in mentionRanges and B2 446-466 in mentionSegments) are replaced by MentionScanner.matches(in:candidates:name:). I compared them with MentionScanner.swift:7-32. The sort key (name length descending), the before/after `!isLetter && !isNumber` tests and the advance-by-name-length are the same. The only difference is that the tuples now use `value` for `persona`. No observable change.

B3 1118-1120: B2's inline `.onContinuousHover` / `.onDisappear` block (B2 1157-1193) is now `.modifier(LinkHoverModifier(...))` (LinkHover.swift:6-51), which ProseRunView.swift:24 also uses. I compared them branch by branch. The pointing hand is pushed or popped only when it changes. The head card shows only when the name, URL and persona agree and the threadID changes, and hides otherwise. End and disappear both pop the hand and hide the card. No observable change.

B3 1095-1096 (commit ff5032673 'Fix opening local file links in chat'): InlineText's own decision when the caller passes no hint changed. B2 used `hasLinks ?? !RichLink.linkHosts(...).isEmpty`; B3 uses `hasLinks ?? RichLink.containsLinks(in:streaming:)`. Text whose only links have no host now takes the native LinkParagraphView path instead of VeiledText. Examples are a local path link like `[a](/Users/me/x.swift:12)` and a mailto: link. On the native path, LinkParagraphView.swift's new MarkdownLinkOpener opens the file. Only hint-less callers are affected: headings (303) and the user bubble `InlineText(parts.body, hugsContent: true)` (TimelineRows.swift:122). Paragraphs (312-322) and list items (343) already pass a containsLinks-derived hint.

B3 532 with 115: RichLink.streamingSlots goes from 4 to MarkdownView.streamingSlots (48). MarkdownView.streamingSlots becomes `nonisolated fileprivate` so that RichLink can read it. The comment at 528-530 already promised 'As many slots as MarkdownView keeps parses'; at B2 the value 4 contradicted it. Up to 48 streaming paragraphs now keep their built pretty strings between flushes.

Line shift (checked with a line-by-line diff of B2 against B3): B2 1-415 are unchanged in place. B2 416-469 are rewritten. B2 470-545 move up 41 and B2 546-549 move up 35.
